title.title: A counterexample to the nearby Lagrangian conjecture
title.subtitle: Claim: an exact Lagrangian in $T^*(S^9 \times S^{N-1})$, diffeomorphic to the base, not Hamiltonian isotopic to it

plain: A sheet floating in a space of positions and momenta looks exactly like the floor, yet can't be slid onto it

lines.note: yet not the zero section, moved by a flow

beats.text: Arnold: every such $L$ is the zero section, moved by a Hamiltonian flow
True for $S^1$, $S^2$ and $T^2$. Fifteen years of Floer theory narrowed what $L$ can be
The claimed $L$ carries a 'tube' class, tied to Waldhausen K-theory, that $Q$ lacks

steps: Floer theory showed $L$ matches the base: homotopy, then simple homotopy
The new $L$ matches it even as a smooth shape: it is diffeomorphic
But a finer 'tube' invariant tells $L$ from the zero section

achievement.label: Arnold's nearby Lagrangian conjecture
statement: L \subset T^*Q \text{ exact},\ \ Q = S^9 \times S^{N-1}
achievement.context: Before: true for $S^1$, $S^2$, $T^2$; any such $L$ is simple homotopy equivalent to $Q$
achievement.note: $N$ is some large even number, not explicit; 28 pages for a central conjecture

verify.detail: No catalogued Lean result; 93 in-progress files under OAI/Geometry/NearbyLagrangian
verify.ourCheck: We trust this landmark least of the group; we checked nothing

voice.text: Arnold expected every such sheet to slide back onto the zero section by a flow.
Everything known matches the base, but a finer tube invariant tells them apart.
Claimed: diffeomorphic, yet not slidable back.

sources.quote: For some sufficiently large even N, Q = S^9 x S^{N-1} has a closed exact embedded Lagrangian L in T*Q, diffeomorphic to Q, that is not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section

sources.quote: Fifteen years of Floer theory showed such a Lagrangian is homotopy equivalent to $Q$ (Abouzaid, Kragh)

sources.quote: This is the claim I trust least among the landmarks, for a simple reason: 28 pages to overturn a central conjecture of symplectic topology, with a non-explicit dimension. There are in-progress Lean files under `OAI/Geometry/NearbyLagrangian` (93 files) but no catalogued result.
